title: Ksolves India Ltd - 543599 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Ksolves FY26 revenue rose 18.4% to INR 162.7 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 29.7% from 34.8%; FY27 guided to 18-20% growth.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR 162.7 crore (up 18.4% YoY), EBITDA of INR 48.3 crore at a 29.7% margin, and PAT of INR 34.3 crore, flat with FY25. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 43.03 crore (up 29.1% YoY, 1.7% QoQ) with a 29.3% EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 9.7 crore. Margin compression was attributed to planned investments in ESOPs, leadership, travel and events, DFM product development, and a one-time INR 1.1 crore labour-code impact. For FY27, management guided to 18-20% revenue growth and a 25-30% EBITDA margin, and said it is shifting focus fully to IT services and winding down product spend.

segments.name: IT services
segments.commentary: Core revenue and profit driver; services span ERP, cloud, data, AI, Salesforce and enterprise transformation. Management says 82% of revenue is recurring.

segments.name: Product (DFM)
segments.commentary: Small contributor. About INR 2 crore expensed on DFM development in FY26; two customers sold to, with two or three in pipeline now pushed to June/July. Management says no further big DFM development spend in FY27 and event spend to fall at least 60%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 annual revenue growth guided at around 18% to 20%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 25% to 30%; management aspires to finish at the higher end.
FY26 expense increases (ESOPs, leadership pay, travel/events, DFM, labour-code one-time INR 1.1 crore) described as largely non-recurring.
Dividend payout to continue at 40% to 60% of profits, as no acquisitions are planned in the coming quarters.
Shift toward more fixed-price and outcome-based engagements and continued talent investment in FY27.
capex_capacity: No capacity or capex figures were disclosed on the call.
DFM product development considered complete; no further large DFM investment planned in FY27.
Added ERPNext/Frappe partnership alongside Odoo to broaden ERP offering; installed-base metrics to be shared later by IR.
Multiple specialist data-science resources added for a US-based financial-crime client, supplied as dedicated people rather than employees.
demand_pricing: Q4 growth was held back by delayed POs from UAE customers due to the ongoing war; management said orders are now being released.
Management said deal conversions are strong and demand healthy, though some deals have been delayed.
Clients are migrating from SAP to Odoo to cut costs; a Tanzanian prospect was cited as a further example.
Management said pricing pressure from AI was not the reason for margin decline; no price-cut detail was given.
Management did not give a order-book or pipeline figure when asked.

qa_highlights.question: How much efficiency will AI agents bring to employee costs in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not measured it yet; agents are reducing time and raising output, and agents are being built for repetitive tasks.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover given the marketing and ESOP costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs are described as non-recurring, with some expenses continuing at lower scale; Q4 margin was at the upper end of the guided range and is expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why was DFM product spend not converting, and is there further hope?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expectations were higher than customer acceptance; it sold to two customers, sees limited DFM opportunity, and will focus on services.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide to a wide 25-30% margin band and why slower growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being conservative given geopolitical uncertainty, and that the larger revenue base means the same percentage adds more absolute revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are UAE war-related delays affecting orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; some UAE customers delayed orders, holding Q4 QoQ growth to 1.7%, and POs are now being released.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT grow faster than revenue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited heavy AI, insurance and IT security investment, so the 25-30% margin band is kept; the aspiration is to end at the higher end.

risks_watch: Margin band of 25-30% is wide; FY26 EBITDA margin fell about 5pp, and PAT was flat for several years.
DFM product has generated little revenue; watch whether pipeline deals close in June/July and whether product spend stays down.
Geopolitical disruption (UAE, war) is delaying customer POs; ~77% of revenue is overseas.
Concentration: top 5 clients 40% and top 10 clients 54% of FY26 revenue.
FX exposure: management said about 60% of revenue comes from North America, and the FX tailwind is currently small.
Growth is decelerating to 18-20% from a 29% Q4 YoY pace as the base grows.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the AI-first positioning and the services business, but cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly described guidance as conservative given geopolitical uncertainty. It was evasive on DFM revenue, pipeline size and the ERP installed base.
key_quotes: We remain confident of delivering sustainable growth while continuing to invest for scale.
We exited FY26 at the upper end of the range guided, that is, 29.7% EBITDA margin, which ensures that we reinforce stability.
But unfortunately, we could not generate revenue from that.
25% to 30% is something we are able to manage easily.

growth.why: Management guided FY27 revenue growth of about 18-20% (midpoint 19%) and a 25-30% EBITDA margin, but gave no capacity, order book or pipeline figures to back it; the brief says it did not give an order-book or pipeline figure when asked, and Q4 QoQ growth was only 1.7% due to UAE PO delays.
